state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process` and `Core\Process\Handle` are green: all five `Handle` members have their feature proofs, `wait` included. `HANDLE_WAIT_DOC` is in the plain voice. `Core\Process\Result`, `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

`wait` now stops the child when either pipe reaches `[limits] max_output`. It shares `read_bounded`'s `stop` with `run`. A child that ignored `SIGPIPE` made it hang before. `tests/conformance/core/process-handle-wait-stops-a-child-that-writes-past-max-output.nvst` pins that.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL. Put the commands in a script under `.agent-tmp/` and start it with `wsl.exe -- bash -lc "bash <script>"`. In the script, build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, run `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file>`, and write the `.out` with Write from what it printed. The attacks and benches run on both platforms: they pick `/bin/sh` or `cmd.exe` by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`. A `.nvst` with a `--FILE nvs.toml--` section runs with `target/debug/nvs.exe test <file>`, not `bun nv try`. Any change to `process.rs` makes every `Core\Process*` perf figure stale: `bun nv proofs --record-perf --group 'Core\Process\Handle'` (and `'Core\Process'`) re-measures them, uncommitted tree included.
